title: I forgot my license ID and password. (CLO below 2024.0)
content: * Please note that the below guideline applies to users who are using CLO version below 2024.0. If you are using CLO 2024.0 and above, please sign in with CLO-SET. **Question** I'm using CLO version below 2024.0 and I forgot my license ID and password. What should I do? **Answer** **Find license ID** To find your license ID, please follow the indicated guideline below: 1. Go to CLO website and click on '[Sign in](https://clo3d.com/en/signin)'. 2. If you forgot your ID but remember the email address used for sign-up, please use the email address to sign in. 3. You can find your ID on the [Account page](https://www.clo3d.com/accounts). However, if you forgot both the license ID and the email address used for signing in, please reach out to CLO via [Contact Us](https://www.clo3d.com/support/contactus) page. **Find Password** Please refer to the following article to reset your license password. * [How can I reset my password on CLO Web and the Software?](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/29936192175129-How-can-I-reset-my-password-on-CLO-Web-and-the-Software)
content_description: This webpage provides guidance for users of CLO versions below 2024.0 on how to recover their license ID and reset their password.

title: Transform Pattern
content: **List of Contents** Transform Pattern Select Pattern Select Multiple Patterns Move Pattern Scale Pattern Rotate Pattern **Transform Pattern** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Brn8gLoXpu8 \- Select, move, and scale Patterns. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022750927/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Tranform Pattern.** ** Select Pattern** * **Click ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yu35gVF14Ms \- Click within the pattern to be selected. \- Or, create a marquee box to encompass the Patterns to be selected. Keep in mind that the Patterns need to be fully enclosed within the marquee box in order to be selected properly. * **Lasso Selection ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AjMYnBirTVA \- Double click on the 2D window to activate the **Lasso Selection.** \- Click around the Patterns to be selected to draw marquee box in a desired shape and click the start point again the complete the Lasso Selection. \- The selected Patterns will be highlighted in yellow. \- Similar with selecting Patterns with the marquee box, Patterns should be fully enclosed. **Select Multiple Patterns** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZJV_Jha4HY0 \- While selecting Patterns, hold down the Shift key and select all Patterns you desire to select. **Move Pattern** * **With Mouse ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rfuj9xoNSkU \- Click and drag the Pattern. * **With Arrow Keys ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GVUd3GiyxCY \- Click the Pattern to be moved. \- Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move the Pattern towards the desired direction. \- The Pattern will move in 1cm increments when using the arrow keys on the keyboard. * **Move in Guidelines ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xDPWHJTN2tc \- While click and dragging the Pattern, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to activate the guidelines. \- The Pattern can be moved in a straight line or a diagonal line. **Scale Pattern** * **Scale Manually ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pfpMEd8QIaU \- Click the Pattern to be scaled. The marquee box will appear around the Pattern. \- Click and drag the white point on the marquee box to enlarge or shrink the selected Pattern. * **Scale with Specific Values ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jYjAxV89Bh8 \- After selecting the Pattern and click and dragging the white point on the marquee box, right click on the 2D window. \- The Transform window will appear. \- Enter the desired values to Percentage and Dimension to scale the Pattern with the desired values. **Rotate Pattern ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U4Lvim31Bmo \- Click on the Pattern to show the marquee box. \- Click and drag the white point above the marquee box to rotate the selected Pattern. * **Pivot Point** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8HBDKLMnjGg \- The point at the center of the Pattern appears with the marquee box is the Pivot Point. \- Double click the Pivot Point to activate it. 。 \- Move the Pivot Point to change the fiducial point which the Pattern will rotate on the basis of. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to learn how to effectively select, move, scale, and rotate patterns using various tools and techniques, complete with instructional videos for each function.

title: Compatible with Wacom 3D Pen (ver 6.0)
content: Wacom 3D Pen Settings How to Control View in CLO Recommended Pen and Touch Settings for windows **Objective** Control the view of the screen with the Wacom Pro Pen (2D) and 3D Pen without any key combination. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QKo3Ej02h_s **Location** Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ View Control ▶ **Wacom Pen** ** Operation** **Wacom 3D Pen Settings** 1. Click the **Start** button. 2. Type **Wacom Tablet Properties** and click on the first search result. 3. My devices ▶ Click the tablet connected ▶ Click the Pen settings. 4. In the **Wacom Tablet Properties** Window click on the **Pen** in the tool list. ![image-20201124-124053.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360099288374/image-20201124-124053.png) 5. Click on the plus "+" button to add an application profile. ![image-20201124-124201.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/1500000416982/image-20201124-124201.png) 6. Click on the **Browse** button in the new window to locate CLO executable and click **OK** button. ![image-20201124-124249.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/1500000417002/image-20201124-124249.png) 7. Set the pen button settings according to the recommended configuration for each of them. Wacom Pro Pen 2 | Wacom Pro Pen 3D ---|--- ![2d_pen.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/1500000416682/2d_pen.png) | ![3d_pen.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/1500000424761/3d_pen.png) How to Set Space Bar: Click the dropdown menu ▶ Keyboard ▶ Modifier ▶ Keys ▶ Check on 'Space Bar' **** **How to Control View in CLO** 1. Control the view in the following way. **Move** | Hold down the middle button while hovering, move the pen on the tablet. ---|--- **Zoom** | Hold down the middle button while the pen tip is touching the device and move the pen in the vertical direction. **Rotate** | Hold down the bottom button while the pen tip is touching or placing close to the device, move the pen to rotate. **Simulate** (Pro Pen 3D Only) | Press the top button once to turn on the simulation and press once again to turn it off. **Select Mesh (Brush)** (Ver 6.1) | When using the Select Mesh (brush) tool, resize the area where the mesh is selected based on the pressure of the pen on the tablet screen. **※Note:** Use another key (e.g. Alt) on the keyboard with the pen to control the view in the 5.2 or lower versions. **** **Recommended pen and Touch Settings for Windows.** 1. Click the **Start** button. 2. Type **Control Panel** and click on the first search result. 3. Switch the Control Panel **display mode** to a **small icon**. 4. Click on **Pen and Touch** settings. **Double-tab** | Double-click (Default Value) ---|--- **Press and hold** | Select the row ▶ Click ‘**Settings** ’ ▶Check off ‘**Enable press and hold for right-clicking**. **Pen Buttons** | Check on both menus below. * Use the pen button as a right-click equivalent. * Use the top of the pen to erase ink (where available).
content_description: Explore optimal Wacom 3D Pen settings for seamless view control in CLO without key combinations, enhancing your design experience.

title: Select/Move/Transform Pattern
content: **List of Contents** Select Move Transform/ Rotate ### **Objective** Select Patterns to move, transform and rotate. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115012734588/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png)Transform Pattern** **Operation** **Select** 1. Select the tool indicated. 2. Click a pattern or hold down the Shift key to multi-select patterns. → The corresponding pattern is selected. 3. Or, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass all Patterns to be selected with a marquee box. → All Patterns inside the marquee box are selected. **※ Note:** Right-click on the pattern ▶ **Select All Sewn**(Ctrl+Alt+A) menu, the pattern and the sewn pattern are automatically selected (**ver 7.3**[**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53142367595033)**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=eLzxKwcLkP1K5On5&t=2728)) **Move** 1. Select the tool indicated. 2. Click and drag the Pattern to be moved or use the [arrow keys](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000376767-%EB%B0%A9%ED%96%A5%ED%82%A4%EB%A1%9C-%EC%9D%B4%EB%8F%99) on keyboard. 3. Hold down the Shift key or Ctrl key (Mac: command) while moving the Pattern. → The Pattern can be moved in precise vertical, horizontal, or diagonal lines, or in its slope. 4. Or, right click or hit F1 key (Mac: Ctrl) while moving the Pattern to type in distance moved. **Transform/ Rotate** 1. Select the tool indicated. 2. Select the Pattern. → The pivot and scale guide appear. 3. Double click the pivot point to activate and transform or rotate based on the pivot point, Click and drag a point or rotation point on the scale guide. → The Pattern is transformed and rotated based on the activated pivot. **※ Note:** * To select point or segment, use the ![______.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/24377127279513) [**Transform Point/Segment**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004423068-%EC%A0%90-%EC%84%A0%EB%B6%84-%EB%B3%80%ED%99%98) tool. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for selecting, moving, transforming, and rotating 2D patterns within the design interface.

title: What is the difference between CLO for Individual and CLO for Enterprise?
content: **Question** What is the difference between CLO for Individual and CLO for Enterprise? **Answer** The licensing policies, features, and services are divided based on user types. CLO for Individual is strictly for individual personal use ( e.g. as a hobby) or individual commercial use (e.g. as an individual freelancer, a one-person company, sole proprietor, etc). Any company with more than one employee must use CLO for Business. Please refer to the compared plans at the bottom of the [plans page](https://www.clo3d.com/plans).
content_description: This web page clarifies the distinctions between CLO for Individual and CLO for Enterprise, outlining licensing policies and intended user types for each option.

title: CLOFAB
content: **Open CLOFAB** **Fabric Information** **Map** **Physical Property** **Save Fabric** #### Digitize fabrics quickly and precisely with enhanced CLOFAB tools Built to integrate seamlessly with the new CLO zFab Kit, our hardware-based fabric digitization system. [ » Explore CLO zFab Kit](https://zfabkit.clo3d.com/) #### **Open CLOFAB** 1. Go to the **Fabric** tab in the Object Browser. 2. If you want to create a new fabric, click ![CLOFAB.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942965148569) button in the top-right corner. 3. To edit an existing fabric, click ![More.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949364889) button next to the fabric and choose **Map** or **Property**. #### **Fabric Information** 1. At the top of **CLOFAB** , enter the fabric name, supplier, and owner. * All information is linked with the information entered in the **Property Editor.** #### **Map** Seamlessly generate maps with scanned or captured images. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949365657) **Open and Crop** 1. Click the ![Open Map.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949367449) button to open your map images. **✨Tip:** If the files follow the [naming rule,](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/44150981805849-Import-All-PBR-Maps-Once#01JWB8QJXE4CZJ4ABC2CZ8RM4P) PBR maps in the same folder will be automatically opened together. 2. Crop your fabric image to remove any background before tiling. 3. Drag the corners or edges of the crop box to keep only the fabric area and remove any unnecessary background before tiling. 4. Press **Enter** or click ![View OK Hover.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942965152793) button to apply and move on to tiling. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949365657) **Auto Tiling** 1. Select the type of repeat pattern. **Pattern Type** | **Description** ---|--- **Plain/Irregular** | Fabrics with a single solid color of fabrics with irregularly scattered patterns.![Plain.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942965155097) **📝Note:** This option analyzes the fabric using the normal map and only works when a normal map is included. **Repeat** | Fabrics with evenly repeating patterns. ![Repeat.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942965155865) 2. Click and drag on cropped image to define a repeat section. **✨Tip:** Auto Tiling works best **when your selection includes about four repeats** , providing the best balance between accuracy and speed. ![Repeat12.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949372185) → The system automatically analyzes the selected area, displays the optimized repeat section as a grid, and previews the repeated result. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949365657) **Manual Tiling** When you want to specify an area manually, switch to Manual Mode and adjust it directly. 1. In the Settings panel, uncheck the **Tiling** option. Or click ![BTN Texture Auto.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949374361) **Switch Mode** button at the bottom right of the selected area. 2. Click and drag to define a repeat section. You can refine it by dragging the corner or edge points to freely shape it into a polygon. 3. Click ![Toggle Check.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942965160857) **Apply** button at the bottom right of the selected section. → The repeat result is previewed. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949365657) **Post-processing** 1. If the tiled fabric looks uneven in brightness, adjust it with the **Equalize** option in the Adjustment panel. ![Equalize.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942965162009) ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949365657) **Apply** 1. When the map is ready, click the **Apply** button to apply it to the fabric properties. **✨Tip:** After applying the map, it will also appear in the physical property preview, allowing you to check both the map and the physical properties at the same time. #### **Physical Property** Simply enter your Fabric Type, Composition and Density to quickly create new accurate fabrics ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949365657) **Create** 1. Click the **Physical Property** tab to switch. 2. Select a fabric type. * You can quickly find a type by typing its first letter on your keyboard in the fabric type list. 3. Select the composition and enter the value (%). ![Composition.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49945934590105) * Basic refers to the primary composition used for the selected fabric type, while Additional refers to compositions that can be combined as extras. → The fabric is draped based on the entered values and previewed. 4. You can check and adjust each physical property value directly in the **Advanced Details** at the bottom if needed. **✨Tip:** If no map is applied to the fabric, you can apply a default map provided for each fabric type by clicking it. Click again to remove it. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949365657) **Set Options** 1. Click **![Cylinder.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949377049)Model Type** button at the top left of the preview and set the preview shape to: Cylinder - Circle / Square, or Dummy - Cape. 2. Click **![Lock Camera.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49942949377817)Lock Camera** button to lock the view adjusted. #### **Save Fabric** Save the created maps and physical properties as a fabric file. 1. Click the **Save** button at the bottom left of **CLOFAB**. 2. Set the options. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Preview Image** | Select the image type to preview the fabric. By default, the fabric’s map image is applied, but you can also add your own image if needed. **Save with Textures** | Save the fabric file along with the map images. For PBR maps, only the existing maps can be selected and saved. 3. Click **OK** and choose a folder to save the file.
content_description: Create, edit, and save detailed fabric information and maps efficiently with CLOFAB's advanced digitization tools integrated with the CLO zFab Kit.

title: Sewing Tension
content: **Sewing Tension** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KXPNHZjz29M \- Adjust sewing Tension to improve 3D Garments’ fit. \- Select the ![Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003396367/Toolbar_Common_Sewing_Edit.png)**Edit Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Select the Sewing Line which the sewing Tension needs to be adjusted. \- Selected Sewing Line’s properties appear in the Property Editor. * Strength : Type in a value to adjust selected Sewing Line’s Tension Strength. * Ratio : Adjust the Tension Ratio to express how various types of Sewing method influence garment drapes. **※****Note: ** The maximum Tension Ratio is 200%.
content_description: This web page provides a guide on how to adjust sewing tension for improved fit in 3D garments using the Edit Sewing tool in CLO 3D software.

title: Avatar (AVT) Open/Add/Save
content: **List of Contents** **Open/Add Avatar** **Save Avatar** **** Model (*.dae or *.obj), sizing data (*.avs), pose (*.pos), motion (*.mtn), accessory (*.acc), bounding volume (*.pan), all avatar-related files such as arrangement points (*.arr) can be saved and loaded into one file (*.avt). **** #### **Open/Add Avatar** 1. Click the File ▶ Open/Add ▶ **Avatar** in the top menus. 2. Select an avatar file. → Open/Add Avatar pop-up window appears. 3. Set the details and click **OK**. **Load Type** | Open | Load your avatar. ---|---|--- Add | Add your avatar. Load as Morph Target | Load the avatar as a morph target. **Translation** | X | Move horizontally based on the center of the 3D garment window. Y | Move vertically based on the center of the 3D garment window. Z | Move forward and backward based on the center of the 3D garment window. Unit | Select the unit of travel distance. **📝 Note:** When adding an avatar, arrangement point is maintained individually for each avatar. **** #### **Save Avatar** 1. Click the File ▶ Save As ▶ **Avatar** in the top menus. → An open file window appears. 2. Specify the location to save the garment file and enter a name and click **Save** to save it. **📝 Note:** * If multiple avatars are loaded, select one avatar and save it as an *.avt file. * When changing the file type to **Encrypted Avatar File(*.avte)** in the Avatar Save window, save it as an encrypted file that cannot be restored to other 3D files and avatar files (AVT).
content_description: This web page provides clear instructions for users on how to open, add, and save avatar files in various formats, ensuring efficient management of avatar-related data within a 3D environment.

title: [Fit Map] Strain Map
content: **** Check how much the garment or fabric stretches under external stress as a percentage. **** 1. Click and hold the ![Fit Maps Off Hover.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/56769397284889) **Fit Map** icon, and select ![Fit Maps Strain Map Hover.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/56769382270745) **Strain Map**(Alt + 7). → Shows how much the garment is stretched as a percentage. 2. Adjust the settings in the Strain Map window. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Global** | Global Mode uses the same scale in the Strain Map, making it easy to see how much a pattern has stretched from its original shape, regardless of fabric type. **Range** | The Strain Map divides the range from the base 100% (no strain) to your defined maximum into 8 segments. **Blue:** Indicates 100% stretch, meaning no strain or deformation. **Red:** Indicates the defined maximum (e.g., 120%), representing the upper limit of stretch. **Gradation:** Values between 100% and the maximum are linearly calculated and expressed as a smooth color gradient. **📝****Note:** You can manually adjust the colors by clicking the each color chip. **Fabric** | Fabric Mode uses each fabric’s stretch limit in the Strain Map, making it easier to see a more accurate and realistic fit. **Range** | The Strain Map divides the range from 100% (no strain) to the fabric’s maximum stretch into 8 segments. **📝****Note:** Each color chip can be selected to manually adjust the colors. **Stretch** | The wearable stretch limit is automatically calculated and applied based on each fabric's physical properties. The stretch limit is the point where the fabric can no longer stretch comfortably under a standard level of force, meaning the garment becomes too uncomfortable to wear. For example, stiff fabrics reach this limit with minimal stretch, while flexible fabrics can stretch much more before reaching their capacity. **📝****Note:** You can manually adjust the maximum stretch as needed. 3. Click a point on the simulated 3D garment to see detailed values at that location. **Dominant Direction** Indicates the specific direction (Warp, Weft, or Bias) that is closest to its stretch limit. **Actual Strectch** Shows the raw physical stretch percentage in the Dominant Direction. **Force** Calculates how close the fabric is to its maximum stretch capacity, where 100% represents the fabric's defined limit. Exceeding 100% means the fabric has been stretched beyond its defined capacity.
content_description: Explore how much your garment or fabric stretches under stress by using the Strain Map tool to visualize and analyze stretch percentages and limits.

title: Measuring a Garment in the 3D Window
content: New garment measures can be placed with the tools **Linear Measure (Garment)** and **Circumference Measure (Garment)**. With **Edit Measure (Garment)** , existing garment measures can be selected, edited, and deleted. These tools function exclusively in the 3D window. # **Location** # **3D Toolbar ▶** **Edit Measure (Garment)![Edit Measure \(Garment\) inactive tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53807775919897)** **Linear Measure (Garment)![Linear Measure \(Garment\) inactive tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53807821052697)** **Circumference Measure (Garment)![Circumference Measure \(Garment\) inactive tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53807821053721)** 1. The linear and circumference measuring tools are grouped into one tool group. 2. Keep your left mouse button pressed on one of them to pop up the submenu. * * * **Main Menu ▶ 3D ▶ Measurement ▶** **Edit Measure (Garment)** **Linear Measure (Garment)** **Circumference Measure (Garment)** # **![Edit Measure \(Garment\) active tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/54065675198105)****Edit Measure (Garment)** Click on a 3D garment measure to edit. → The selected measure is now highlighted. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. **Linear Measure (Garment)** | **Circumference Measure (Garment)** ---|--- **Name** | Rename the measure. | **Name** | Rename the measure. **Length** | Check the length of the measure. | **Surface Length** | Check the length of the measure. **Square Width** | Modify the width of the square that appears at the end of the measure. | **Circle Diameter** | Modify the circle diameter that appears around the measure. # **![Linear Measure \(Garment\) active tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/54065686021529)****Linear Measure (Garment)** 1. Click once at the beginning point of where you want to start the measure. → A green dot and rectangle appear. 2. Click again to define the endpoint of the measure. → A linear measurement is created and instantly displayed. 3. If you hold Shift on the keyboard, the direction of the measure can be defined in angled increments of 45° instead of freehand. # **![Circumference Measure \(Garment\) active tool icon](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/54065686021657)****Circumference Measure (Garment)** Click on an area to measure its circumference. → A circumference measurement is created and instantly displayed.
content_description: This web page provides essential tools for accurately measuring and editing garment dimensions in a 3D environment.

title: Slash and Spread
content: **List of Contents** Slash and Spread Create Slash Line Rotate Pattern **Slash and Spread** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IzVgGn3N-z0 \- Create a Slash Line inside a Pattern to divide, rotate, and edit the Pattern. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022743268/mceclip0.png) **Slash &Spread** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Patterns ▶ Edit ▶**Slash &Spread.** ** Create Slash Line** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5wzgrEnj0Bk \- To divide and rotate the Patterns, the Slash Line must be created first. \- The Slash Line can be created on the Pattern outlines. \- Click on the Pattern outline to create the start point. The start point of the Slash Line will be the fiducial point where the Pattern will rotated on the basis of. Drag the mouse on click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. \- Baselines and Internal Lines can also be used as Slash Lines. 。 **Rotate Pattern** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kYwCxjbo2jU \- Click the half of the Pattern that will be rotated. Hover the mouse over the half and when the Pattern is highlighted in light-blue, click to select. When the half of the Pattern is selected, it will be highlighted in yellow. \- Move the mouse cursor to preview the Pattern after the modification. Rotate the Pattern to spread or clip Patterns. \- Move the half of the Pattern as desired and click to complete the modification. \- Baselines and Internal Lines can also be used to rotate Patterns. \- Or, when moving the half of the Pattern, right-click to access the Spread window. Enter the desired values to Distance and Angle and click OK. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for using the "Slash and Spread" tool in pattern editing, featuring detailed instructions and instructional videos for creating slash lines and rotating patterns.

title: Grading

title: Fill (ver 6.2)
content: **List of Contents** Duplicate Property ### **Objective** Create a realistic puffy garment by setting the fill type and weight. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VuJyDM7hYHs **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Fill** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4409935066265/mceclip0.png) **Fill** **Operation** **Duplicate** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated.** ** 2. Click the piece to be applied or, Click anywhere in the 2D window ▶ Drag your cursor to select the pieces within the marquee. ** **→ The duplicated pieces appear on the mouse cursor. 3. Select any grey quilt lines to turn on the quilting effect. **Property** 1. Click the puffy pattern piece. **→** Filer Property appears in the Property Editor. 2. Once the puffy properties are set, simulate the garment.** ** **Property**** ** | **Description** ---|--- **Filer** | Type | Choose the type of filler. Weight | Enter the weight of the filler. **※Note:** Select multiple pattern pieces to set the total weight. The weight of each piece is calculated and distributed proportionally. Quilting Distance | Enter the quilting distance. ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4409111186457/mceclip2.png) **※Note:** Fill Volume is calculated based on the Quilting Distance and the Weight. title: glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB) File
content: Import or export glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB) files. ![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947024654617) [Watch Video](https://youtu.be/NHUPJ8ceaqs) **** #### **Import** 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ **glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB)** 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. 3. Configure the settings and click **OK** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Open Type** | Open or add new files. **Object Type** | **Load as Avatar / Trim** | Load a GLTF/GLB file as an avatar / trim. **Arrangement Points** **Auto Generate** | It automatically creates a Bounding Volume/Arrangement Points suitable for GLTF/GLB. **Scale** | Type in the Scale or select the desired unit. * Commonly used default unit for GLTF file is Meter. **Axis Conversion** | Invert each axis of the OBJ as needed. **** #### **Export** 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ **glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB)** 2. Select the desired saving path and click **Save**. 3. Configure the settings and click **OK**. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Object** | **Select All Avatars/ Patterns/ Graphics/ Trims** | Select or deselect objects to be exported. **Single/ Multiple Objects** | Export the object as a single or multiple objects. **Thick/Thin** | Choose to export the object with the thickness or not. **Combined UV Coordinates** | A combined UV coordinates are also exported. **Option** | **Light** **(Except for Render Lights)** | Export along with lights **Garment Animation** | Export garment's animation. **Avatar Animation** | ## ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/49947024656537) Export Joint or Cached avatar animation. **Scale** | Select the unit or the size of the object. * Commonly used default unit for GLTF file is Meter. **Axis Conversion** | Invert each axis of the OBJ as needed. **Animation** | **Entire Region** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/61161883700249) Exports the entire range where animation keys are set. **Play Region Only** | ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/61161883700249) Exports only the animation within the specified playback range. **File** | **Save Colorway** | Choose whether you export colorway or not. Combine to One File/Multiple Files | Choose whether you combine all colorways into one file or create separate files for each colorway. **Save with glTF-Embedded (GLTF Only)** | Save textures as the glTF-Embedded format which includes texture files. **Save with Zip Files (ZIP)** **** | **Diffuse Color Combined on Texture** | When color is applied to the texture, the color is blended into the texture when exporting. **📝Note:** Since the color is diffused to the UV map when the Combined UV Coordinates is selected, the menu is hidden. **Exclude Ambient Map & Color (Modo)** | Ambient Map and color are excluded when exporting.. **📝Note:** Since ambient maps and color are automatically excluded, the menu is hidden. **Save with MetaData (XML)** | Save garments' patterns (mesh), physical properties, and sewing information as MetaData (XML). **** #### **Extensions** **Property** | **Description** | **Required** ---|---|--- **Reflection Factor** | Reflection intensity of PBR material. In CLO, it has defaulted 15(0.15). Other engines and SW is defaulted 100(1.0) like the real world. | No, Default: 1.0
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions for importing and exporting glTF 2.0 (GLTF/GLB) files, including detailed configuration options to optimize your 3D assets for various applications.

title: Garment Fit Maps
content: **Objective** Utilize the four Garment Fit Maps in the 3D window to check the fit of garments. ** Location** 3D Window ▶ hover the mouse over the 7th icon ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window ▶ hover the mouse over the 7th icon → Four Garment Fit Maps appear. 2. Refer to the table below and select the desired view icon. **Icon** | **Description** ---|--- Stress Map | Force along the fabric grain per unit area of the fabric that causes garment deformation; appears in a range of colors and numbers. The Stress Map appears in a total eight colors: Red indicates the strongest stress (100kPa) while blue indicates zero distortion (0.00kPa). Other numbers in between are expressed as a gradation of two colors. Strain Map | Garment's stretch rate due to external force; appears in percentage. The Strain Map appears in a total of eight colors: Red indicates 120% of stretch rate while blue indicates 100% (no stretch). Numbers in between are expressed as a gradation of two colors. Fit Map | The Fit Map shows tightness of the garment. **Can't Wear** appears in red indicating a non-wearable area. **Very Tight** appears in orange indicating a very tight area. **Tight** appears in yellow indicating a slightly tight area. Pressure Map | External pressure exerted by garments onto avatars. → Based on the selected icon, the Stress Map, Strain Map, Fit Map, or Pressure Map appear on the garment.
content_description: Explore the four Garment Fit Maps in the 3D window to accurately assess and visualize the fit of garments by hovering over the designated icon.

title: Create and Edit Zipper
content: **List of Contents** Create Edit Unzip / Zip Set Options **** Create and Edit Zippers quickly and easily. **** #### **Create** 1. Click ![Zipper.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115008480088) **Zipper** tool in the 3D toolbar. 2. Click on the 3D garment or 2D Patterns where the Zipper is attached, then move the cursor. →Based on the direction the cursor was moved, the segment where the Zipper appears is highlighted in light blue. 3. Double click on the desired endpoint for the Zipper. → One side of the Zipper is created. 4. Click on the Pattern outline where the other side of the Zipper is attached, then move the cursor. → Based on the direction the cursor was moved, a blue point appears indicating the same length as the first half of the Zipper that was created. 5. Double click on the blue point. → The Zipper is now complete along with a Puller, a Slider, and a Stopper. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59568160571289) The Zipper tape will also be displayed in 2D window. Users can create/edit sewing and internal lines on zipper patterns. In the 3D window, zipper patterns can be moved using the gizmo or dragged during simulation. 6. Activate the ![Toolbar_3D_Simulation.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115008384087) → The Zipper simulates being closed. 7. While creating the zipper, press **Esc/C****trl+Z** to cancel all actions, or **Delete/Backspace** to undo the last action. #### **** #### **Edit** 1. Click **![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/24447291991705)****Edit Zipper** tool in the 3D toolbar. 2. Click the end point of the zipper ▶ Drag in direction to be edited, then Click on the end point of the opposite zipper ▶ Drag it the same way. → A blue dot is displayed at the same point as the opposite length. 3. Drag to the blue dot. → Both lengths of the zipper are modified. **** #### **Unzip / Zip** 1. Click ![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51925976193305) Select/Move tool in the 3D toolbar. 2. Click & drag on the slider. → The selected slider is highlighted in yellow. 3. Continue to drag the slider. → The slider follows and moves along with the cursor. 4. Release the mouse at the desired position. → The slider is moved to the new location. 5. Activate the ![Toolbar_3D_Simulation.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51925976206233) **Simulate** tool. → The zipper simulates and zips/unzips based on the new location. **** #### **Set Options** 1. Right-click on the 3D zipper using ![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51925976193305) **Select/Move** tool. 2. Click an option as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Delete** | Delete the selected Zipper. **Reverse** | Reverse the sewing direction of the zipper tape on the side you right-clicked. **Flip Normal** | Flip the surface of the zipper tape on the side you right-clicked. **Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern** | Duplicate the selected zipper to the corresponding symmetric pattern. This option is available only when the zipper is placed on a symmetric pattern or when it does not cross the center line of a half symmetric pattern. **Deactivate/ Freeze** | Deactivate or freeze the selected Zipper. **Reset Slider Arrangement** | Reset the slider's position and angle to default. **Show/Hide** | Show or hide the Slider/ Puller/ Stopper.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for users to efficiently create, edit, and manage zippers in their 3D garment designs.

title: How to Solve "Error Code 400" Login Failure
content: This article explains how to solve login failures due to "**Error Code: 400** " and/or "**Error Code: 10002** ". **Technical Background** Starting in March 2024, [**the CLO team has integrated the different accounts of users**](https://landing.clo-set.com/allatonce) using CLO software, CLO-SET, and CONNECT into one, and the CLO software have changed the login via CLO-SET webpage instead of entering ID and password in the login window. This policy will be applied from CLO version 2024.0, and previously released CLO 7.x or 6.x versions will run by entering ID and password. After the account integration, if the previously-used-user-login-information and the newly-integrated-user-information do not match, or if old-user-information is stored in the web browser being used, the CLO software login will fail and an error message will be displayed. **Problem Situations** ![001_ErrorCode_400.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36701673887641) ![002_now_signed_in_to_CLO-SET.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/36701673892761) * Launched CLO, but get an error message instead of logging in. * Successfully logged in to CLO-SET on a web browser, but get an error message. * * * **Causes and Solutions** **In case of security app blocks CLO's internet connection** * If an antivirus, firewall, or web monitoring program installed on your computer blocks the CLO software from communicating with the Internet, CLO login will fail. * Change the Internet connection of CLO software to "Allow" in the detailed settings of your antivirus, firewall, or web monitoring program, and then run the CLO software again. **CLO software does not have sufficient file read and write permissions** * [**Refer to this web post**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/17074279996697) to grant administrator rights to the CLO software and then run CLO again. **CLO-SET password error** * [**Refer to this web post**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/29936192175129) to reset your CLO-SET password and then run CLO again. **Web browser security policy or web browser cache error** * Web browsers with strict security policies or specific web browsers may have problems accessing the CLO-SET webpage. In this case, please try using a different web browser instead of the one you were using. Also, check again your web browser's security settings. * You may be experiencing problems logging into CLO-SET due to an outdated web browser cache. In this case, clear your cache and try logging in again. This [**saved-search**](https://www.google.com/search?q=how+to+clear+web+browser+cache&oq=how+to+clear+web+browser+cache&gs_lcrp=EgZjaHJvbWUyBggAEEUYOdIBCDg1OTFqMGoxqAIAsAIA&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8) will help. **CLO software configuration error** * The internal configuration and settings of the CLO software may have been damaged during the CLO Live Update and install. * [**Refer to this web post**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/16218721000601) to completely uninstall the CLO software and fresh install it using the latest installer. Don't forget to back up your working files to a safe place before uninstalling CLO software. * * * **Read More** * Learn more about [**CLO-SET Account Integration**](https://landing.clo-set.com/allatonce) here. See also [**CLO Account Integration User Guide**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/28934650069785). * If you have followed the steps above but are still unable to log in, please send us your screenshot or error code via [**Contact Us**](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus/technical).
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide to resolving login issues related to "Error Code: 400" and "Error Code: 10002" following the integration of user accounts in CLO software, ensuring a seamless login experience.

title: Graphic Properties
content: **List of Contents** **Set Properties** **Set Options** **** Set the graphic properties. #### **Set Properties** ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51790077104665) **By Graphic Style;**_Applies changes to all graphics that use the same style._ 1. Click the Graphic Style in the Graphic tab in the Object Browser. 2. Set properties in the Property Editor. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | **Name/Item No.** | Enter a name or an item number of the graphic. **Classification** | Assign the graphic type among Embroidery, Logo, Print, Wash (Jeanologia). **Teckpack** **(CLO-SET)** | Check whether to include the graphic in the tech pack. Assign the classification of the graphic as per its purpose. **Material** | **Print Type** | Set the print type of the graphic (Crack, Vintage Distress, Golden Foil). When you select the Blend with Base Fabric type, all PBR maps (Normal, Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, Metalness maps) of the fabric applied to the pattern are automatically applied and blended with the fabric. Otherwise, you can selectively apply only specific maps by checking the 'Use the same map as the fabric' option for each map. Set the graphic's [material](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015998728-%EC%9E%AC%EC%A7%88-%EC%9C%A0%ED%98%95), [texture](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000471388-%EC%9B%90%EB%8B%A8-%ED%85%8D%EC%8A%A4%EC%B2%98-%EB%84%A3%EA%B8%B0), [color](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000716427-%EC%9B%90%EB%8B%A8-%EC%83%89%EC%83%81), and [transparency](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000512488-%ED%88%AC%EB%AA%85%EB%8F%84-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95). **Graphic Transformation** | Lock Size: Lock the graphic's size and material map scale. **(New in 2026.1)** Adjust the width and height of the graphic to transform its size. ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/51790077104665) **By Each Graphic;**_Applies changes only to each selected graphic, even if they share the same style._ __ 1\. Click the Graphic using ![Transform Graphic.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53267500551833) **Transform Graphic** tool in the 2D toolbar. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Graphic Configuration** | **Face** | Place the graphic on the front, back, or both sides. **Tile** | Repeat the graphic in its original size along the X-axis, Y-axis, or across the entire pattern. **Over Seamline** [![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/26258156519577) Watch Video](https://youtu.be/bV6e36l_95A?si=AWD9r_QdGkHTvdJB&t=4271) | Place the graphic on the seam of patterns. * Graphic does not appear when the difference of the seam is over the allowable extent. * Graphic may not be matching when it is placed over the curves. It this case, deactivate this option and adjust the graphic manually. * Graphics are also created for patterns sewn in two layers, such as pockets. **Fur Trimmer** | Show the graphic clearly when using [Fur (Render)](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/search/click?%3D--d3e47a82d57d92fcfaa10db63e9249ce765c4e8e) and [Fur_Strand](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/search/click?%3D%3D--23de7be8c49f912b7f9f0d961a4e0d06a1ce05a8) materiels. No fur is generated in the graphic area. Example: Fur Trimmer = Turn on vs. Turn off ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55403276077337) ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/55403276085657) **Graphic Transformation** | Lock Placement: Lock this graphic's position, angle, Z-offset, and configuration on this pattern. **(New in 2026.1)** Adjust the rotation angle and Z-offset of graphic. **2D Measurements** | Click the desired measurement option to check the position within the 2D pattern in dimensions. **Transform Graphic** | Precisely place graphics by entering exact position values. #### **Set Options** 1. Right-click on the Graphic using ![Transform Graphic.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/53267500551833) **Transform Graphic** tool in the 2D toolbar. 2. Select the option as needed. **Options** | **Descriptions** ---|--- **Delete** | Delete the selected graphic. **Copy/ Paste** | Copy, Paste, and Mirror Paste the selected graphic. **Order (2D)** | Set the placement order of the graphic. **Rotate** | Set the rotation angle of the graphic. **Tile** | Repeat the graphic in its original size along the X-axis, Y-axis, or across the entire pattern. **Revert to Original Size** | Restore the transformed graphic to its original size. **Flip** | Flip the graphic horizontally or vertically. **Lock Placement** | ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/59568847778329) Lock this graphic's position, angle, Z-offset, and configuration on this pattern. **Trace as Internal Shape** [![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/26258156519577) Watch Video](https://youtu.be/3FTUcfpFrWI?si=j50eaGqv_JOeGc_Y) | Trace the graphic as an internal shape according to its outline. **📝Note:** The clearer the image, the more accurately it is recognized. For complex and colored images, tracing is based on the outermost outline. **Custom Measurements** [**![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/26258156519577)**Watch Video](https://youtu.be/u3AWgMtT_9U?si=mkdbFzGglJTUaSY9&t=199) | Measure the distance from a specific point of the graphic to its outline and create a measurement. The created measurement is displayed in the Property Editor, and you can rename or delete it as needed.
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide to setting and customizing graphic properties and options in your design software, enabling users to efficiently manage graphic styles, placements, and transformations.

title: Skive
content: ### **Objective** Add skiving effect on desired parts of a Pattern or all Patterns (ver2.3.0). ** Location** Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ **Skive** **Operation** 1. Select a pattern or an internal shape to express skiving with ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005592427/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern** or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005592407/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern **tools. → Its properties appear in Property Editor. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) ▶ Bond/Skive ▶ **Skive** → The select Pattern/Internal Shape is now being displayed in a semi-transparent grey color. → A scrollbar appears, displaying the physical property of the pattern from the value range of one ('1') to one hundred ('100') in **Percentage (%)**. 3. Move the scrollbar to adjust as desired. 4. Activate the ![Toolbar_3D_Simulation.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024827668/Toolbar_3D_Simulation.png) **Simulate**. → The area of the internal shape is now being displayed softer as if it has been shaved down.
content_description: Learn how to apply a skiving effect to patterns and internal shapes in the Property Editor for enhanced design flexibility in version 2.3.0.

title: Adjust Avatar Size
content: **Objective ** Create an avatar with your own measurements. As CLO Avatar Editor is powered by thousands of real body scan data, even measurements not assigned by users automatically adjust to the most realistic body shape. ** ****Location **** **Main Menu ▶Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶**Avatar Size** ** ****Operation** 1. Load an [Avatar (.avt)](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002687268). 2. Select the tool/menu indicated.** **→ Measures appear on the Avatar. The editable measures appear in black, whereas the non-editable measures appear in grey. 3. Refer to below graph and adjust the Avatar as needed. **Option** | **Description**** ** ---|--- **Avatar Size ** | Easily select the size of the avatar in the Avatar Size Editor. **Total Body**** **| Shape the overall body type with Avatar's height and chest width. In order to get realistic shapes for body parts without assignable measurements, use the Total Body option to create an overall shape and then insert measurements under the Details option. **Height** | Assign Avatar's height. Because each person has a different head size, it is most accurate to create a full body shape based on HPS Height or Inseam. Total Height is the least accurate and is not recommended. **Total Height** | Insert the height measured from the ground to the head. **HPS Height** | Insert the height measured from the ground to the neck. **Inseam** | Insert the height measured from the ground to the crotch. **Proportion (ver 7.2 [![Youtube Icon.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/26258263192089)](https://youtu.be/CwB8_ad328M?si=QRMvussOAoDZ_aMm&t=1447))**** ** | Adjust the ratio of the avatar's upper and lower body. **Inseam** | Once the height between the floor and the legs is entered, the upper body automatically adjusts proportionally. **CF Neck to Waist** | Once the height from the Front Neck Point to the waist is entered, the lower body automatically adjusts proportionally. **Width** | Shape the overall body type based on Bust/ Under Bust Circumference, Weight. **Weight (ver 7.1)** | Enter the weight to set its overall body width. After entering the weight, select the desired total body shape and it will be changed to the corresponding body shape. **Details**** **** **| Configure Avatar's detailed measurements. A small error may be generated when entering measurements, and the error appears right next to each measurement. The actual applied measurements are displayed in the [Avatar Measurement](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055394453-Avatar-Measure-ver-6-0-) , so edit them more accurately by referring to them. **Basic** | Adjust the value of the basic body measurements. Body measurements that cannot be adjusted are automatically changed to realistic body shapes based on actual data according to the adjusted measurements. **Advanced** | Adjust the value of detailed body measurements. Advanced has more adjustable body measurments, but this may be more unnatural than the Basic option, as other measurements are not automatically adjusted and are fixed to the entered values. **Simple (ver 7.1)** | When changing the width based on weight, simply adjust the size of the minimized body measurements. **Show All Measurements** | Click the button at the top right of Details to check the all measurements. **Open/ Save** | Open or save the avatar size measurements. **Reset** | Reset the avatar's size to the default state.
content_description: Create a personalized avatar by customizing your measurements with the CLO Avatar Editor, which utilizes real body scan data for realistic adjustments.

title: Create Binding
content: ### **Objective** Easily create Binding along Pattern Outlines. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Binding ▶ **Binding** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Binding** ** Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location.** **→ Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Binding can be created appear in dashed lines. 2. On a 3D Garment or 2D Pattern, click the start point and double click where you want to finish the Binding. → Binding is created on the selected segment. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. → The pattern of the Binding is displayed in the Print Layout Mode. (ver 7.1)
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide for users to easily create and manage Binding along Pattern Outlines within a design software interface.

title: Press
content: **List of Contents** Press Simulate Sewing Line Type **Press** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vhk5txLTy-I \- Press 3D Garments to flatten bulged Seamlines when more than two layers are sewn together. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022649048/mceclip0.png) **Press** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment ▶ **Press -**With the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022649048/mceclip0.png) **Press** tool selected, navigate to the 3D window and click on the Pattern to be flattened. \- The selected Pattern will disappear. \- Click the other Pattern sewn to the first Pattern. \- The Pattern that was clicked for the first time will appear again. ** Simulate** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=celMronJyc0 \- Activate the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022649088/mceclip1.png) **Simulation** tool. \- The bulged Seamline will be flattened. ** Sewing Line Type** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1wlwej6nY_c \- When the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022649048/mceclip0.png)**Press** tool is used to a Pattern, its all Sewing Lines’ Sewing Line Type changed to Turned(ver4.1.0). Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Press and Simulation tools in Clo3D to effectively flatten bulged seamlines in 3D garments, complete with instructional videos and step-by-step instructions.

title: Self-Service Refunds Within 24 Hours of First Billing After Free Trial
content: CLO offers self-service refunds under specific conditions. If you're an individual user, you may request a refund within 24 hours of your first billing after the free trial ends. During this 24-hour window, your refund request will be automatically approved. ⚠️ Please note: ➤ The self-refund option is only available within 24 hours of your first paid billing after the free trial. #### #### **Refund Eligibility** * Applies only to individual users * Valid for the first paid billing after the free trial * Refund must be requested within 24 hours of that billing #### #### **How to request a refund:** You can request a refund in either of the following ways: Option 1: From your account 1. Go to your **[Subscription]** page 2. Click "Request Refund" within 24 hours of your first charge 3. Your subscription will be cancelled and your refund will be processed instantly Option 2: From the billing confirmation email 4. If your subscription has just renewed after the free trial, you’ll receive a confirmation email. 5. This email includes a "Request Refund" button that is valid for 24 hours only. 6. Clicking the button will cancel your subscription and trigger an instant refund. #### #### **Didn't request a refund but got a confirmation?** If you receive a refund confirmation email without having requested one, or notice any suspicious activity, please reach out to CLO via [Contact Us](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus).
content_description: This web page provides guidelines for individual users on how to request self-service refunds within 24 hours of their first billing after a free trial.
